events.title: Dominique de Villepin Declares A 2027 Presidential Bid
events.summary: Former prime minister Dominique de Villepin announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election at a press conference in Paris on 20 November. He presented himself as an alternative to Macronism, La France insoumise and the Rassemblement national, and denounced what he called a situation of decay in the country.

events.title: Public-Sector Unions Hold A Nationwide Strike Day Over Pay
events.summary: All public-sector unions called France's 5.8 million public employees to strike and demonstrate on 17 November for immediate pay rises, during the debate on the 2027 budget. Marches took place in Paris and other cities. Fewer than 3 percent of central-government employees went on strike, according to Le Monde. On 20 November the unions called a further strike day for 1 December, joined by private-sector unions.

events.title: Cost-Of-Living Protests Enter A Fifth Weekend With Smaller Crowds
events.summary: Demonstrations took place across France on 14 November for the fifth Saturday of the movement against the rising cost of living, which began with secondary-school students. Marches on child protection, opposition to what protesters call a police "licence to kill", wages and school resources converged on a single march in Paris. Turnout and tensions were somewhat lower than on previous weekends; RFI reported 219 arrests and 10 police officers slightly injured nationwide by the evening, and 45 arrests in Paris.

events.title: Teddy Riner And Éric Zemmour Enter 2027 Presidential Race
events.summary: Teddy Riner, a five-time Olympic judo champion, announced on 9 November that he will stand in the 2027 presidential election. On 10 November Éric Zemmour, president of the far-right Reconquête party, formally declared his candidacy on TF1; he had said in September that he would run. They join Marine Le Pen, who launched her campaign in October.

events.title: France Blames Iran's Revolutionary Guards For Supermarket Cyberattacks
events.summary: French authorities blamed Iran's Revolutionary Guards on 9 November for the 12 October cyberattack that sent refrigerator temperatures soaring at about 700 of France's 10,000 supermarkets, and Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said she had opened an investigation into Shahid Kaveh, a cyber unit of the Guards. Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Iran's ambassador would be summoned and that France would seek European-level sanctions. Iran's foreign ministry called the accusations "baseless and one-sided".

events.title: Police Block Banned Rally As Protests Enter Fourth Weekend
events.summary: About 146,000 people protested across France on 7 November, including 46,000 in Paris, according to the Interior Ministry, while unions put the figure at 250,000. Police blocked a banned Yellow Vest rally in Paris, and about 70,000 security personnel were deployed nationwide. It was the fourth consecutive weekend of cost-of-living protests.

events.title: Bus Crash In Ain Kills Two, Including A Child
events.summary: A regional bus carrying schoolchildren and other passengers left the road near Lent, in the Ain department, on 6 November, struck trees and landed in a ditch, killing a 7-year-old girl and an 18-year-old. Sixteen people were injured, three of them seriously. Preliminary tests found no trace of alcohol or drugs in the driver's blood.

events.title: Hundreds Of Thousands Join National Day Of Strikes And Marches
events.summary: A national day of strikes and demonstrations over wages and the cost of living took place across France on 5 November, organised by the main trade unions and joined by students and Yellow Vest protesters. The Interior Ministry estimated about 575,000 participants at roughly 200 demonstrations, including about 65,000 in Paris. At least 448 people were detained, the ministry said, though most marches were peaceful.

events.title: Cyberattack On Crédit Mutuel Arkéa Diverts More Than €100 Million
events.summary: French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirmed on 4 November that a cyberattack had allowed fraudulent transactions. Reports put the amount diverted at more than 100 million euros, with one estimate as high as 118 million, and said the funds were converted into cryptocurrency. The bank said its customers would not suffer any financial loss, and an investigation has been opened.

events.title: Third Weekend Of Cost-Of-Living Protests Draws Smaller Crowds
events.summary: About 320,000 people took part in a third Saturday of cost-of-living protests across France on 31 October, including 70,000 in Paris, according to the Interior Ministry, a smaller turnout than on the previous two weekends. The ministry reported 565 arrests by the evening, and 779 by the next day.

events.title: Marine Le Pen Launches 2027 Presidential Campaign
events.summary: National Rally leader Marine Le Pen launched her campaign for the 2027 presidential election at a rally in Orléans on 25 October. She is campaigning while appealing a conviction for embezzling European Parliament funds. On the economy she pledged spending restraint and lower business taxes.

events.title: More Than 1,300 Arrested As Second Wave Of Protests Sweeps France
events.summary: About 410,000 people joined a second nationwide day of cost-of-living demonstrations on 24 October, according to the Interior Ministry, while the CGT union put the figure at around 800,000. Police used tear gas to disperse crowds in several places, including Lyon. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the next day that 1,314 people had been arrested.

events.title: Gunman Kills One And Wounds Seven In Paris Suburbs
events.summary: A gunman opened fire in Trappes and La Verrière, in the Paris suburbs, on 23 October, killing a 26-year-old man and wounding seven other people. The national anti-terrorism prosecutor's office (PNAT) is leading the investigation into what it treats as a racist attack. The 39-year-old suspect was transferred to a Paris court to appear before an anti-terrorism investigating judge; prosecutors said he admitted the shootings but denied they were racist. In November, investigators said a list of four public figures found at his home did not point to any plan of violent action against them.
